report.summary: Start by addressing L1 immediately, as it drives the largest revenue loss of $104.6k at the checkout to payment info step for new visitors. Next, focus on L2 ($67.5k lost revenue) and L3 ($32.7k lost revenue) to resolve early-funnel drop-offs for first-time shoppers. Finally, address L4 ($18.4k lost revenue) and L5 ($12.0k lost revenue) to capture remaining checkout optimizations.

leaks.headline: New visitors convert at 43.9% from checkout to payment info, lower than the rest of the shop.
leaks.what_is_happening: For 5,976 sessions entering this step, new visitors convert at 43.9% compared to 81.7% for the rest of the shop. This gap leads to 1,530 lost purchases and $104.6k in lost revenue.

likely_causes.cause: Forced account creation or mandatory registration prompt at checkout.
likely_causes.why_plausible: First-time visitors who are forced to create an account before entering payment details often abandon checkout.

likely_causes.cause: Unexpected shipping fees revealed at the payment entry step.
likely_causes.why_plausible: New shoppers seeing calculated shipping costs for the first time may drop out before submitting payment info.

what_to_check: Run a conversion report comparing guest checkout users against account creation users during checkout.
Watch session recordings of new visitors dropping off between checkout and payment info to observe form friction.

experiments.name: Prominent Guest Checkout
experiments.hypothesis: If we display a prominent guest checkout option, then checkout → payment info conversion for new visitors will increase, because first-time buyers avoid account creation friction.
experiments.metric: checkout → payment info conversion for new visitors

confidence.reason: L1 represents the highest financial loss ($104.6k) with a large conversion gap between 43.9% and 81.7%.

leaks.caveat: Since returning visitors almost always convert better than new ones due to higher intent, part of this gap is intent, so the lost revenue is an upper bound.

leaks.headline: New visitors convert at 22.3% from view item to add to cart, underperforming the rest of the shop.
leaks.what_is_happening: Out of 52,232 sessions reaching product views, new visitors convert at 22.3% versus 34.7% for the rest of the shop. This bottleneck causes 987 lost purchases and $67.5k in lost revenue.

likely_causes.cause: Lack of visible product reviews or trust badges on item pages.
likely_causes.why_plausible: First-time visitors unfamiliar with the brand need social proof before adding products to their cart.

likely_causes.cause: Unclear sizing details, specifications, or stock availability.
likely_causes.why_plausible: New shoppers who cannot quickly confirm product details will refrain from adding items to cart.

what_to_check: Check product page add-to-cart conversion rates segmented by new versus returning visitors.
Review mobile and desktop product detail pages to test page load speed and clarity of the add-to-cart button.

experiments.name: Product Page Trust Badges and Reviews
experiments.hypothesis: If we display star ratings and money-back guarantees near the add-to-cart button, then view item → add to cart conversion for new visitors will increase, because first-time buyers gain trust in the product.
experiments.metric: view item → add to cart conversion for new visitors

confidence.reason: L2 impacts a large volume of 52,232 sessions resulting in $67.5k in lost revenue.

leaks.caveat: Since returning visitors almost always convert better than new ones due to higher intent, part of this gap is intent, so the lost revenue is an upper bound.

leaks.headline: New visitors convert at 20.0% from visit to view item, lagging behind the rest of the shop.
leaks.what_is_happening: Across 261,238 sessions, new visitors convert from visit to view item at 20.0% compared to 25.4% for the rest of the shop. This gap generates 478 lost purchases and $32.7k in lost revenue.

likely_causes.cause: Generic homepage layout that fails to surface popular products.
likely_causes.why_plausible: First-time visitors arriving on the homepage need clear visual cues to navigate to specific item pages.

likely_causes.cause: Mismatch between acquisition landing pages and initial user expectations.
likely_causes.why_plausible: New traffic entering top-of-funnel pages may bounce if product categories are not immediately visible.

what_to_check: Review landing page click-through rates to product pages for new visitors across top traffic channels.
Test homepage category navigation on mobile devices to evaluate visual clarity for first-time users.

experiments.name: Featured Product Category Grid
experiments.hypothesis: If we feature top-selling product categories directly on the main landing page, then visit → view item conversion for new visitors will increase, because first-time visitors can quickly locate relevant items.
experiments.metric: visit → view item conversion for new visitors

confidence.reason: Although session volume is high at 261,238, the overall revenue opportunity is $32.7k due to early-funnel drop-off.

leaks.caveat: Since returning visitors almost always convert better than new ones due to higher intent, part of this gap is intent, so the lost revenue is an upper bound.

leaks.headline: New visitors convert at 51.3% from add to cart to checkout, trailing the rest of the shop.
leaks.what_is_happening: For 11,644 sessions entering this step, new visitors convert at 51.3% compared to 59.1% for the rest of the shop. This leakage leads to 269 lost purchases and $18.4k in lost revenue.

likely_causes.cause: Lack of shipping cost estimates or free shipping thresholds inside the cart.
likely_causes.why_plausible: First-time visitors adding items to cart abandon before checkout if final costs remain uncertain.

likely_causes.cause: Unclear or low-contrast checkout call-to-action button in the cart drawer.
likely_causes.why_plausible: New users navigating the store layout for the first time may miss the button to proceed to checkout.

what_to_check: Analyze cart page abandonment reports specifically for first-time visitors.
Examine session recordings of cart views where new visitors do not click the checkout button.

experiments.name: Free Shipping Progress Bar in Cart
experiments.hypothesis: If we show a free shipping threshold progress bar in the cart, then add to cart → checkout conversion for new visitors will increase, because transparent savings incentives encourage starting checkout.
experiments.metric: add to cart → checkout conversion for new visitors

confidence.reason: L4 accounts for $18.4k in lost revenue across 11,644 sessions.

leaks.caveat: Since returning visitors almost always convert better than new ones due to higher intent, part of this gap is intent, so the lost revenue is an upper bound.

leaks.headline: Organic first-touch visitors convert at 56.8% from checkout to payment info, lower than the shop average.
leaks.what_is_happening: Among 3,412 sessions, organic first-touch visitors convert at 56.8% from checkout to payment info versus 63.4% for the rest of the shop. This results in 156 lost purchases and $12.0k in lost revenue.

likely_causes.cause: Prominent promo code field prompting users to leave checkout.
likely_causes.why_plausible: Organic search visitors arriving at checkout may exit the site to search external pages for discount codes.

likely_causes.cause: Missing payment security badges for users discovering the store via search.
likely_causes.why_plausible: First-touch organic visitors who lack brand awareness need extra security assurances before entering payment details.

what_to_check: Check checkout drop-off rates for organic search landing traffic.
Inspect session recordings of organic users at the checkout step to see if they highlight or copy text from discount code inputs.

experiments.name: Collapsed Promo Code Field
experiments.hypothesis: If we collapse the promo code input behind a text link during checkout, then checkout → payment info conversion for organic visitors will increase, because shoppers will not leave the checkout flow to look for coupons.
experiments.metric: checkout → payment info conversion for organic visitors

confidence.reason: L5 has the smallest financial impact among identified leaks at $12.0k in lost revenue.

leaks.caveat: Channel indicates how the user first arrived at the shop, so attribution reflects intent differences inherent to organic search acquisition.
